newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clyde says production up 9.0 pct in '96.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clyde says production up 9.0 pct in '96.

text.p: Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc, the target of a hostile bid by Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, said on Thursday its actual production for 1996 rose some 9.0 percent to 41,117 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Clyde said production was set to rise to over 60,000 barrels per day by 1999 as it stepped up its defence against Gulf Canada's 432 million stg bid, which it considers too low.
Clyde Petroleum said operating cash flow rose an estimated 29 percent last year to 127 million stg. Discretionary cash flow (after tax and interest) climbed 37 percent to 113 million stg.
"Our strategy has delivered record production, reserves and results," said Clyde's chairman Malcolm Gourlay.
"The inadequacy of the Gulf Canada offer has been underlined by the new information released today," he added.
Clyde said Gulf Canada's cash offer of 105 pence per share equates to a "mere" 3.8 times the 1996 discretionary cash flow per share.
It cited an independent consultant -- J.S. Herold -- as saying that an appropriate cash flow multiple would be in the range of 5.3 to 6.4.
This would imply a trading range of 146 to 177 pence, Clyde said. The shares actually firmed 1/2 a penny to 119-1/2, reflecting market hopes of a counter bid.
Gulf Canada's bid, launched on December 18, failed to take into account Clyde's "impressive" 1996 performance, its rising production and financial strength, Clyde said.
"An independent Clyde can deliver a far better return for shareholders," said managing director Roy Franklin.
